rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.minimizer_full_support_actual
rows.plain: Support and moments for the minimiser
rows.annotation: The first conjunct, `μ.support = univ`, is the support claim. Here `μ` is supplied with `IsStieltjesMeasure γ μ`, and its underlying type `Time` is the interval $[0,1)$.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.gaussianProduct
rows.annotation: `Measure.pi` assigns a copy of `standardGaussian` to each coordinate. In the SK model the coordinate type is `Fin n × Fin n`, and the Hamiltonian uses the coordinates with $i<j$.

rows.name: OAI.SKValue.hamiltonian
rows.annotation: The two sums run over all ordered pairs, with the `if i < j` branch keeping each coupling once. Lean stores a configuration as a Boolean function and uses `spin` to obtain the factors in $\{-1,1\}$.

rows.fidelity_note: Defines the finite-n expected maximum per spin; it does not assert the existence of the displayed limit.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.groundStateSequence
rows.annotation: `sSup (range (hamiltonian n J))` takes the maximum over the finite spin configurations at fixed disorder $J$. The integral averages that maximum over the Gaussian product measure, and the factor $(n:\mathbb R)^{-1}$ gives the $n$th term whose limit is displayed.

rows.fidelity_note: Names the limit candidate via limUnder; convergence is supplied by the next theorem.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.groundStateValue
rows.annotation: `limUnder atTop groundStateSequence` names the limit candidate as $n\to\infty$. Convergence to that value is the separate statement `groundStateSequence_tendsto`.

rows.name: OAI.SKValueG.groundStateSequence_tendsto
rows.note: Proves that the sequence actually converges to the named value.
rows.annotation: The `Tendsto` statement identifies `groundStateValue` as the limit of the sequence of expected optima per spin. The filter `atTop` is on the size parameter $n$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.OrderParameter
rows.annotation: `val` has domain `Time`, the subtype $[0,1)$. The `integrable` field concerns its zero extension to $\mathbb R$, so it expresses the time integrability in the definition of $\mathcal U$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsStieltjesMeasure
rows.annotation: `Set.Iic t` is taken in `Time`, so its real interval is $[0,t]$. The right-hand side uses `ENNReal.ofReal` because the mass is measured in the extended nonnegative reals.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.SupportDeterministic.IsStieltjesMeasure.cdf_add_Ioc
rows.note: The same increment formula is written additively in nonnegative extended reals.
rows.annotation: Lean writes $\gamma(a)+\mu((a,b])=\gamma(b)$ in the extended nonnegative reals. Since both cumulative values are finite, the difference in the paper is the mass of `Ioc a b`.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.parameterMeasure
rows.note: The construction explicitly adds this initial Dirac mass.
rows.annotation: `Measure.dirac ⊥` puts mass at the least element of `Time`, which is $0$. The multiplier is `ENNReal.ofReal (γ.val ⊥)`, giving the initial mass needed for $\mu_\gamma([0,t])=\gamma(t)$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Time
rows.annotation: `Time` is a subtype of $\mathbb R$, so the topology used by `Measure.support` is the relative topology on $[0,1)$. In that type `Set.univ` denotes the whole overlap interval.

rows.fidelity_note: Lean explicitly treats gaps $(a,b)$ with $0\le a<b<1$; the sentence also allows relatively open endpoint gaps.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.SupportDeterministic.constant_on_support_gap
rows.annotation: `hgap` requires every point of the real interval `Ioo a b` to lie outside the support, with $0\leq a<b<1$. The conclusion gives a single $c\geq0$ for every point of that open interval.

rows.fidelity_note: Defines the Parisi functional, the last clause of the display; it does not state the PDE or terminal condition.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.parisi
rows.annotation: `value W γ 0 0` supplies $\Phi_\gamma(0,0)$, and the interval integral supplies the penalty $\frac12\int_0^1t\gamma(t)\,dt$ using the zero extension of $\gamma$. This definition implements the functional clause of the display.

rows.fidelity_note: States only $\Phi(1,x)=\lvert x\rvert$, using the scalar model; it does not state the PDE or Parisi functional.
rows.name: OAI.SKValue.phi_terminal
rows.annotation: Setting the time argument of `phi` to `1` gives $|x|$ for every real $x$ and every admissible coefficient. This supplies the terminal-value clause in the scalar model, without stating the PDE or defining the functional.

rows.fidelity_note: Gives the right time derivative before one via compactValueRate; the terminal value and functional definition are separate.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_derivative_hasDerivWithinAt_right
rows.plain: Right time derivative of spatial derivatives
rows.annotation: At $0\le t<T<1$, the right time derivative of $\partial_x^m\Phi_\gamma(t,x)$ is the $m$th spatial derivative of `compactValueRate`, with $m=0$ giving the PDE time derivative. The set `Ioi t` specifies approach from the right, including times when $\gamma$ jumps.

rows.fidelity_note: Expands the compact time rate as the PDE right-hand side; it does not by itself assert that $\Phi$ has that derivative.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.compactValueRate_eq
rows.annotation: On $0\le t\le T<1$, `compactGradient` is $\Phi_x$ and `compactCoeff` is $\gamma(t)$, making the right side the displayed PDE expression. This definitional equality expands the rate without asserting that $\Phi$ has that time derivative.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value
rows.annotation: For $0\le t\le1$, the supremum ranges over expected payoffs of controls progressive for Brownian increments after $t$ and bounded by one in absolute value. In `controlPayoff`, the terminal absolute value is reduced by the quadratic cost $\frac12\int_t^1\gamma(s)\alpha_{s-t}^2\,ds$.

rows.fidelity_note: Lean proves convergence of its specified finite-step/log-cosh family `approxValue`, not arbitrary bounded monotone approximations.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.approxValue_uniform
rows.annotation: The theorem gives uniform convergence of `approxValue` over all $0\leq t\leq1$ and $x\in\mathbb R$. That family uses the source’s finite-step coefficients and its smoothed absolute-value terminal data.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_coefficient_stability
rows.annotation: For $t\le1$, changing $\gamma$ to $\eta$ changes the value at any field $x$ by at most $\frac32$ times the $L^1$ distance of their zero extensions on $[t,1]$. The bound is uniform in $x$ and requires no minimality hypothesis.

rows.annotation: The hypothesis `hmin` supplies a minimiser in the scalar model. Lean concludes $P_*=\mathcal P(\gamma)$ for that supplied parameter, and attainment of the minimum in the display is a separate input.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gradient
rows.annotation: In `deriv (value W γ t) x` the values `W`, `γ` and `t` are held fixed. Differentiating in `x` gives the paper’s $\Phi_x$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvature
rows.annotation: `curvature` applies `deriv` to `gradient W γ t` in its remaining argument `x`. The two derivatives are spatial, giving $\partial_x(\Phi_x)=\Phi_{xx}$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.BrownianSystem
rows.annotation: `law` and `isProbability` specify the probability measure for expectations, while `B` has nonnegative real time. The field `brownian` asserts that this measurable real process is standard Brownian motion under that law.

rows.fidelity_note: Defines the SDE in integral form with $X_{0}=0$ and measurability; it does not define $q$.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsDiffusion
rows.annotation: The second conjunct is the integral SDE with $X_0=0$, imposed almost surely for every $0\le t\le1$ on continuous paths. The first conjunct requires progressiveness for the natural Brownian filtration, while the definition of $q$ is elsewhere.

rows.fidelity_note: Defines q as the squared-gradient expectation; it does not assert that X solves the SDE.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.squareMoment
rows.annotation: `squareMoment` integrates the square of `gradient` along `X` against `W.law`, giving $q(t)$. The definition takes `X` as an arbitrary process.

rows.fidelity_note: Provides an adapted solution for the given Brownian system; uniqueness is a separate theorem.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.diffusion_isDiffusion
rows.annotation: The constructed `diffusion W γ` satisfies `IsDiffusion`, including progressiveness for the given Brownian motion and the almost-sure integral equation on $[0,1]$. This establishes existence, with uniqueness supplied separately.

rows.fidelity_note: Assumes a process satisfies IsDiffusion and proves almost-sure pathwise equality with the constructed process; existence is separate.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.diffusion_uniqueness
rows.plain: Uniqueness for the given Brownian motion
rows.annotation: `hX` assumes another solution driven by the same `W`, and the conclusion gives one event of full probability on which both paths agree for every $0\le t\le1$. The time quantifier lies inside the almost-sure statement, so the exceptional set is independent of time.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsMinimizer
rows.annotation: `IsMinimizer` compares `parisi W γ` with `parisi W η` for every `η : OrderParameter`. This expresses global minimality for the supplied `γ`.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.full_support
rows.annotation: The last conjunct of `FullSupportConclusion` gives both identities for every `X` satisfying `IsDiffusion` and every `t : Time`. The proof transfers the identities from `diffusion W γ` by almost-sure equality at each such time.

rows.fidelity_note: Expands the proposition named by full_support; this definition does not itself prove any of its clauses.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.FullSupportConclusion
rows.note: Read the final quantified clause for the two displayed moments; full_support supplies its proof.
rows.plain: Full Stieltjes support, strict increase and moment identities on [0,1)
rows.annotation: The last clause quantifies over every `X` satisfying `IsDiffusion` and every `t : Time`. It gives the two moment identities at all $0\leq t<1$, including zero.

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem gives $u(t,0)=0$ for every $0\le t<1$ and every order parameter, not just the minimiser at time zero.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.gradient_zero
rows.annotation: Specialising to $t=0$ gives the selected $u(0,0)=0$, while the declaration gives $u(t,0)=0$ for every $0\le t<1$ and every admissible $\gamma$.

rows.plain: Spatial formula for the second derivative
rows.annotation: `actualJet` uses unscaled derivatives of $\Phi$, so the integral is $\mathbb E[\Phi_{xxx}^2-2c\Phi_{xx}^3]$. Multiplication by $c^2$ produces the first displayed polynomial after `stripSecond` has been identified with $q''$ on a constant interval.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvatureMoment_hasDerivAt_on_constant
rows.annotation: The differentiated function is `curvatureMoment`, which equals $q'$, so this identifies `stripSecond` with $q''$ at interior points of $(a,b)$ where $\gamma=c$ and $0\le a<b\le T<1$. The spatial integral in the display requires the separate expansion of `stripSecond`.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripThird_eq_actual
rows.plain: Spatial expression in the coercive inequality
rows.annotation: With `actualJet` denoting unscaled spatial derivatives along the diffusion, `stripThird` is $\mathbb E[\Phi_{xxxx}^2-12c\Phi_{xx}\Phi_{xxx}^2+6c^2\Phi_{xx}^4]$. Once it is identified with $q'''$ on a constant interval, multiplication by $c^2$ gives the second displayed formula.

rows.fidelity_note: Identifies q‴ with stripThird on a constant interval; the spatial expansion and q″ formula are separate.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvatureMoment_deriv_hasDerivAt_on_constant
rows.annotation: The derivative of `deriv (curvatureMoment W γ)` is `stripThird W γ T c t` at interior points of a constant interval with $0\le a<b\le T<1$. Since `curvatureMoment` is $q'$, this supplies the time-derivative identification for $q'''$, before expanding its spatial expression.

rows.fidelity_note: Supplies the non-strict bound for stripThird; identifying q‴ and proving strict positivity require the additional linked lemmas.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.stripThird_coercive
rows.plain: Third-order lower bound c² E[a⁴]/1000 at continuity points with c > 0
rows.annotation: At a continuity point $0<t\le T<1$, the inequality bounds $\gamma(t)^2$ times `stripThird` below by $\gamma(t)^4\mathbb E[a^4]/1000$, without assuming a constant interval. Identification with $q'''$ and strict positivity are additional steps.

rows.fidelity_note: Identifies q‴ on a constant interval but does not state the quantitative lower bound.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.curvatureMoment_deriv_hasDerivAt_on_constant
rows.annotation: For $\gamma=c$ on $(a,b)$ with $0\le a<b\le T<1$, this identifies `stripThird` with the second derivative of `curvatureMoment`, hence with $q'''$ at interior points. It supplies the derivative identification, without a quantitative or strict lower bound.

rows.fidelity_note: Gives strict positivity of $\mathbb E[a^4]$ for $t>0$, but not the displayed lower bound for $q'''$.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.actualQuartic_pos
rows.annotation: The fourth moment is of the unscaled curvature $a=\Phi_{xx}$, since `actualJet` at order two is evaluated along `diffusion`. Its strict positivity for $0<t<1$ gives the positive right-hand side after multiplication by $c^4/1000$ when $c>0$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.rational_identity
rows.annotation: The identity holds for arbitrary real inputs and retains `WF₂` among the summands alongside squares and `remainder`. It gives the algebraic decomposition before shape assumptions and integration eliminate that term.

rows.fidelity_note: This proof removes the divergence for a specified Gaussian-type density under explicit shape hypotheses; identifying it with the law of Xₜ is separate.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Heat.gaussian_shape_coercivity
rows.annotation: `hiZero` sets the integral of `certDivergence` over $(0,\infty)$ to zero, using vanishing flux at zero and infinity. The density is `gaussianLogDensity d U` under the listed shape hypotheses, and identifying it with the law of $X_t$ is an additional step.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.Certificate.remainder_lower_bound

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_even
rows.annotation: For each $0\le t\le1$, `Function.Even (value W γ t)` means $\Phi_\gamma(t,-x)=\Phi_\gamma(t,x)$ for every real $x$, including at terminal time.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_convex
rows.annotation: Fixing $t$, `ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (value W γ t)` asserts convexity of $x\mapsto\Phi_\gamma(t,x)$ on all of $\mathbb R$, under the sole time condition $t\le1$.

rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_lipschitz
rows.annotation: The constant in `LipschitzWith 1` gives $|\Phi_\gamma(t,x)-\Phi_\gamma(t,y)|\le|x-y|$ for all real $x,y$, for every admissible $\gamma$ and $t\le1$.

rows.fidelity_note: Supplies uniform bounds for every positive-order derivative on the strip; continuity is supplied separately.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_uniform_derivative_bounds
rows.annotation: The order `m+1` ranges over positive spatial derivatives, excluding $\Phi$ itself. For fixed $W,\gamma,T,m$, one $C\ge0$ works for every $0\le t\le T<1$ and $x\in\mathbb R$, while continuity is supplied separately.

rows.fidelity_note: Supplies joint continuity of all spatial derivatives on the strip; the uniform bounds are supplied separately.
rows.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.value_derivative_continuousOn
rows.annotation: The pair `p` supplies time through `p.1` and the field through `p.2`, so `ContinuousOn` asserts joint continuity of $\partial_x^m\Phi_\gamma$ on the strip. The order $m$ includes zero, hence $\Phi$ itself, and uniform bounds are separate.

rows.annotation: The derivative value `curvatureMoment W γ t` is $\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^2]$, and `Ici 0` makes the derivative at zero one-sided. For $0<t<1$ this is the usual derivative of $q$, for every admissible $\gamma$, without asserting the stochastic differential in the display.

rows.annotation: The subtraction in `val` removes the cumulative mass of a finite submeasure $\nu\le\mu$, and the structure fields establish admissibility of the result. For the paper's perturbation, instantiate this $\nu$ with $\varepsilon(\mu|_K)$ for $0\le\varepsilon\le1$.
